description: The line plot illustrates the evolution of training loss over iterations for six different model configurations, plotted against a linear x-axis labeled “#Iteration” ranging from 0 to 140,000 with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000, and a linear y-axis labeled “Loss” spanning from 2.4 to 3.4 with tick marks every 0.1 unit. The “Vanilla” model (purple line, solid) begins at approximately 3.4 and drops sharply in the first 10,000 iterations to around 2.5, then gradually declines to stabilize near 2.45 by 140,000 iterations. “StrmLLM (n=64)” (blue line, solid) starts near 3.4, decreases more gradually than Vanilla, and plateaus around 2.7 after 80,000 iterations. “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange line, solid) begins at 3.4 and follows a smooth, steady decline to approximately 2.55 at 140,000 iterations. “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green line, solid) starts at 3.4 and consistently remains slightly below SepLLM (n=64), ending near 2.52. “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red line, solid) also begins at 3.4, declines steadily, and achieves the lowest final loss of approximately 2.4 by 140,000 iterations. “SepLLM (n=128)” (dark blue line, solid) starts at 3.4, drops more steeply than the n=64 variants initially, and stabilizes around 2.5 after 100,000 iterations. A faint vertical green line is visible near 10,000 iterations, serving as a visual reference point across all curves. All lines exhibit a consistent downward trend with diminishing returns over time, and no lines intersect after the initial 5,000 iterations.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the change in loss over iterations for different models. The x-axis is labeled '#Iteration' and ranges from 0 to 140,000, while the y-axis is labeled 'Loss' and spans from 2.4 to 3.4. Six models are compared: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128). The Vanilla model exhibits the steepest initial decline, stabilizing near 2.45 by the end. StrmLLM (n=64) shows a slower rate of loss reduction, plateauing at approximately 2.7. SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) demonstrate similar trends, with SepLLM (n=64, H) consistently outperforming SepLLM (n=64) by a small margin. SepLLM (n=64, H/T) achieves the lowest final loss value, roughly 2.4, while SepLLM (n=128) stabilizes at a slightly higher loss of 2.5. The light green vertical line marks a reference point for comparison. Overall, the SepLLM variants exhibit superior performance compared to Vanilla and StrmLLM, with SepLLM (n=64, H/T) achieving the best results.
